study type: Prospective, multicenter, single-arm, open-label, clinical trial
exposure: AEGEA Vapor System endometrial ablation (120-second treatment time)
outcome: Reduction of menstrual blood loss (pictorial blood loss assessment score <=75)
Need for surgical or medical intervention to treat abnormal bleeding
cohort: The study included 155 premenopausal women aged 30 to 50 years with heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) as determined by a pictorial blood loss assessment score >=150, allowing treatment for up to 12-cm uterine sound lengths and nonobstructing myomata.
finding: At 12 months, the primary effectiveness end point (reduction of menstrual blood loss to a pictorial blood loss assessment score <=75) was achieved in 78.7% of subjects, and 90.8% of subjects were satisfied or very satisfied with the treatment.
